topic: What a shorter bus journey conceals
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: What a shorter bus journey conceals
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. The fictional town of Alderport tested a bus lane for six weeks. Its transport office compared twenty morning journeys before the change with twenty afterwards. The average journey fell from thirty minutes to twenty-four. A newspaper described this as a benefit shared by every passenger, but the underlying records supported a narrower claim. An average describes a group; it does not show how each member of that group was affected.

B. At the central stop, buses became more reliable. At the outer stops, however, the timetable was reduced because two vehicles had been transferred to the busiest section. Some passengers waited longer even though their time on the bus fell. The office had measured travel time between stops, rather than the entire door-to-door journey. For someone who waited an extra fifteen minutes, a saving of six minutes on board would not represent an improvement.

C. The comparison also had a seasonal limitation. The first observations took place during term time, whereas the second period included a school holiday. Less traffic might therefore explain part of the difference. Engineers proposed keeping the lane through another school term and comparing similar weekdays. They also wanted to record the median waiting time, which is the middle value when observations are ordered. This would complement the mean rather than replace every other measure.

D. A separate survey reached passengers through an online questionnaire. People who had stopped using the service were unlikely to see it. The survey could describe the views of its respondents, but it could not establish the views of all former users. A more useful evaluation would combine journey records with interviews at outer stops and a check on cancelled services. The council postponed a permanent decision until these additional records were available.

questions.explanation: 依据原文“The average journey fell from thirty minutes to twenty-four.”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。
questions.evidence: The average journey fell from thirty minutes to twenty-four.

questions.prompt: Why did some outer stops lose frequency?
options: Road repairs made the stops inaccessible.
Drivers refused to use the new lane.
Vehicles were reassigned to the busiest section.
answers: Vehicles were reassigned to the busiest section.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“two vehicles had been transferred to the busiest section.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: two vehicles had been transferred to the busiest section.

questions.prompt: Which part of the experience did the original timing omit?
options: The speed of the moving buses.
Waiting and access within the entire journey.
All time spent on the vehicle.
answers: Waiting and access within the entire journey.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“rather than the entire door-to-door journey.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.prompt: The middle observation is called the _____.
questions.explanation: 题干问排序后的中间值名称，可答median；原文中的完整指标名median waiting time也接受。
questions.evidence: the median waiting time, which is the middle value when observations are ordered.

questions.prompt: Who was especially likely to be missed by the questionnaire?
options: People using buses in term time.
People who had abandoned the service.
answers: People who had abandoned the service.
